Kuvitus: aurinkoisena päivänä puutarhan: Illustration: on a sunny day three soap bubbles float above a garden. The surface of the largest bubble has horizontal bands of colour: grey and white at the top, then yellow, orange, magenta, blue and green, and lower down yellow and magenta again. On a table there is a bowl of soapy water and a bubble wand. The colours are calculated from the thickness of the soap film, which increases from the top of the bubble to the bottom.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: saippuak: Schematic picture, not to scale: a soap film in cross-section, with air on both sides. The thickness d of the film is exaggerated, and the rays are drawn slanted so that they can be told apart; the chapter considers light at normal incidence. The ray arriving from above is partly reflected from the upper surface of the film: this is ray 1, and the wave reflected there gets a half-wavelength shift, because the light is reflected from a material of higher refractive index. Part of the light continues into the film, is reflected from the lower surface of the film against air without a shift, and returns through the upper surface into the air: this is ray 2. Ray 2 travels an extra distance in the film, twice the thickness of the film. A weak part of the light continues through the lower surface downwards.
Kaavakuva: kalvosta heijastuneet aallot: Formula picture: the waves 1 and 2 reflected from the film and their sum in two cases. On the left the film is much thinner than the wavelength. Wave 1 is inverted in the reflection from the upper surface, wave 2 is not, and wave 2 has not lagged behind, so the waves are in opposite phase: a crest meets a trough, and the sum is a horizontal straight line, that is, there is no reflected light. On the right the film is so thick that wave 2 travels half a wavelength further. The waves are then in phase, and the sum is a wave of double amplitude, that is, the reflection is strong.
Kuva lasketuista väreistä: valkoisessa v: Picture of calculated colours: the colour of the light reflected in white light from a soap film with a refractive index of 1.33 as a function of the film thickness, at normal incidence. Above, a wedge-shaped film in cross-section, whose thickness grows from left to right from zero to 1000 nanometres (thickness exaggerated). The colour strip starts on the left as black, turns grey-blue, white, yellow, orange and, at about 200 nanometres, magenta, then blue, green, yellow and magenta again. The thicker the film, the paler the colours become. The brightness of the colours has been enhanced: the real reflection is only a few per cent.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kohtisuoraan tule: Graph to scale: the percentage R of light reflected at normal incidence as a function of wavelength from 400 to 700 nm. Uncoated glass with a refractive index of 1.52 reflects about 4.3 per cent at all wavelengths, a horizontal black line. When the glass is coated with a magnesium fluoride layer with a refractive index of 1.38 and a thickness of 99.6 nanometres, that is, a quarter of the wavelength 550 nanometres in the film, the green curve falls to its minimum of about 1.3 per cent at 550 nanometres and rises towards the edges: to about 2.2 per cent at 400 nanometres and about 1.6 per cent at 700 nanometres. The dependence of the refractive indices on wavelength is not taken into account.
Kuvitus: sateen jälkeen asfaltilla on lä: Illustration: after rain there is a puddle on the asphalt, with a thin film of oil on its surface. The film shows winding rings of blue, green, yellow and magenta, because the film is thicker in the middle than at the edges. The colours are calculated for an oil film on water.
